    StartersMainsSweetsDrinks
    StartersSmoked Salmon BliniWarm blini, crème fraîche, salmon roe and dill.Passed on silver trays, 30th floor, from seven.How to make it16 cocktail blinis100g crème fraîche150g smoked salmon50g salmon roe1 small bunch dillWarm the blini on a tray at 180°C.Top each with crème fraîche and a curl of smoked salmon.Finish with salmon roe and a dill sprig.Pass around on a tray straight away.Rosemary Roasted NutsCashews and almonds, brown sugar butter, cayenne.Same recipe as the back of the limo.How to make it30g butter1 tbsp brown sugar2 tsp chopped rosemary1/4 tsp cayenne pepper1/2 tsp salt150g cashews150g almondsMelt the butter with the sugar, rosemary, cayenne and salt.Toss through the cashews and almonds and spread on a lined tray.Roast at 170°C, stirring halfway.Cool so they crisp, then serve warm in a glass bowl.MainsRoast Beef on Soft RollsRare top round, horseradish cream, rocket, pickled onions.Christmas Eve supper, served at 8:30.How to make it1kg beef topside1 tbsp Dijon mustard1 tsp cracked black pepper1 tsp salt2 tbsp horseradish150ml sour cream8 soft rolls60g rocket100g pickled onions, slicedRub the beef with Dijon, pepper and salt.Roast at 200°C until 52°C inside.Rest, then shave thin.Stir the horseradish into the sour cream.Split the rolls, spread with horseradish cream and fill with beef, rocket and pickled onions.SweetsCream-Filled Snack CakesVanilla sponge fingers piped with marshmallow cream.A night patrol favourite. Take two for the road.How to make it125g soft butter300g caster sugar5 eggs, 3 whole and 2 whites1 tsp vanilla extract200g self-raising flour80ml milk50ml waterBeat the butter with half of the sugar, beat in the whole eggs one at a time and the vanilla, then fold in the flour and milk.Bake in a lined 20 x 30cm tin at 180°C.Cool and cut into 12 fingers.Boil the rest of the sugar with the water to 118°C and pour into the egg whites, whisking hard until thick and glossy.Split the fingers and pipe the cream inside.DrinksOld FashionedBourbon, brown sugar, orange bitters, one big cube.A drink for Mr Cowboy. Yippee-ki-yay.How to make it2 tbsp brown sugar2 tbsp hot water240ml bourbon8 dashes of orange bitters1 orange, for peel strips4 large ice cubes1 bag ice for stirringDissolve the sugar in the hot water for a syrup.Stir the bourbon, syrup and bitters with ice in a jug until very cold.Strain into 4 heavy tumblers over one large ice cube each.Squeeze orange peel over each, rub the rim and drop it in.
